- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.0) — model fails to recognize downward momentum, often missing early drops.
- Lag in correction: model delays mean reversion after strong sentiment shifts — prices often dip below forecast before rebounding.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves: model overreacts to recent highs, leading to inflated forecasts in the following days.
- Horizon bias: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) and underestimate late (last 5–7 days) — adjust for asymmetric decay.
- Sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment is stable or neutral, reduce forecast volatility; if sentiment is volatile, increase smoothing to avoid overfitting to noise.
